summary: The subject held frozen at the dispatched digest across every measurement, start and end, and the prompt held too. My turn-1 blocker C2-D057-01 is repaired at the root: a new path, the turn-1 findings dispositioned in a table, and 'Do not edit this subject after dispatch' written into the entry itself. On content the entry is clean and I re-derived it rather than carrying my earlier clearance forward: all six cited digests match live bytes including my own turn-1 verdict, all ten eligible-row pairings reproduce against the adopted register, the RB-DR005-V2-A1 rider is genuinely in adopted D-039, and DR-006/007/009 have no adopted Route B selection while DR-010 is route C. The revision from the bytes I previously cleared loses no tokens and leaves clauses 1-3 byte-identical at be6af59c, with every addition narrowing rather than widening. One note records that this same path moved once before the dispatch was re-pinned, which is signal about the repair's first application rather than a defect in these bytes.

notesRecorded.location: review-cycle history, not the entry's content
notesRecorded.observation: This turn-2 path moved once after being dispatched and before the dispatch was re-pinned. The turn-2 prompt file initially pinned cab483b5493f98588b471a55eb3688e3146767bc295bf51667ab92fa3f417bdc and I measured exactly that at first contact; the file then became 30b7b29978f926821fae66aecb7c3a45d2b7bf664adab0b0cbe69de4cd20daf3, 109 lines where it had been 83, and the prompt file itself changed from 3b5c21d3 to b2f75c0b. The dispatch was then re-pinned at 30b7b299, and from that point the subject has been stable across every measurement I have taken, start and end.
notesRecorded.whyItIsNotAFinding: This review binds 30b7b299, the digest the dispatch freezes, and against that baseline start equals end. The motion predates this dispatch rather than occurring inside it, and it was a sanctioned re-pin rather than uncontrolled drift — the content it produced is the folding of my own turn-1 finding. Grading these bytes for a dispatch they superseded would be objecting to something outside this review's window.
notesRecorded.whyItIsWorthRecording: The entry's own disposition table accepts C2-D057-01 as 'New path; start=end required', and the new path then moved once before settling. That is useful signal about the repair's first application. Counting the family: D-054 turn 1's subject moved during review, D-057 turn 1's subject never matched its dispatch, and this path moved once before re-pinning. The control works when applied — D-054 turn 2 and this dispatch both held — and what it still needs is coverage of the window between writing a dispatch and the reviewer's first measurement.

whatIVerified: Subject digest at start and end: 30b7b29978f926821fae66aecb7c3a45d2b7bf664adab0b0cbe69de4cd20daf3, measured three times at start and again at end, all identical and all equal to the digest the dispatch freezes. The prompt likewise held at b2f75c0bd97efe6b9117b30012d5cd018d5a74fe492ae8eecc89be36c2f38db6. The dispatch made start-digest-not-equal-to-end a MUST-FIX and that condition does not arise.

C2-D057-01 is repaired at the root rather than papered over. My turn-1 objection was that the subject was not the dispatched artifact. This turn uses a new path, states its provenance in the entry — 'This is a new frozen path. Turn-1 used coordinator-decisions.D-057.draft.md, which moved during review… Those bytes and verdicts are history' — records the finding in a disposition table as 'C2-D057-01 | MUST-FIX | ACCEPTED. New path; start=end required', and writes the control into the measured-inputs block as 'Do not edit this subject after dispatch.'

My turn-1 verdict is pinned correctly at 17f940d67a9f0b9363f21352beb79bec31599715e9ba87c620509af2d69ee011, and the Codex turn-1 verdict at 004127e7685ee5b23849fce5e56dcff22f3f08c20b33cdad2eac39d8f5f7ad8e, confirmed by hashing without opening. The D-054 user amendment is pinned at c274d140f15e207ad3cd4a00f6dc29292832f3c1c664ba55e9715ffff235462f and matches its file; the D-054 commit 29670ed exists in git log.

The attack 'cited digests do not match live bytes' fails on all six: COORD fb1189620f7ac653d0d92c0fe223e3854806336a5738da70e2580ffad96b89a5 and file 08 6547e6ace2ae61e664af0f65059b66c2cb3d0539d64f6687aba04f8f54dc4cd7 both match live, plus the four above. The COORD pin is the current post-D-054 value rather than a carried-forward one.

I re-derived the substance rather than relying on having cleared the predecessor bytes. The attack 'this entry itself grants owner authority' fails five ways: the decision-type line 'Authority is user-made adopted D-054, not this file'; the header's '**Does not** grant owner authority'; clause 1 titled 'This file does not grant' with 'Overturning this entry does not overturn D-054'; the rejected alternative 'Repeat the grant in this file'; and the reversibility clause 'C-D057 revokes these mechanics. D-054 remains until C-D054.'

The attack 'this entry itself discharges condition 1' fails: clause 6 states 'This entry records no row. Readiness effect zero. File 08 is not edited here', and the Readiness effect section reads 'Zero.'

The attack 'silent SATISFIED' fails: the header carries '**Does not** mark SATISFIED', clause 4 forbids the later owner-recording from marking the row SATISFIED, and clause 5's only other use is DR-001's existing standing.

The attack 'same-commit coordinator + owner recording' fails twice: clause 2 requires the coordinator recording to be 'already ADOPTED and separately committed (D-000 clause 4)' with 'Same-commit bundling… is forbidden', and the alternatives reject it on the same authority.

The attack 'owner record of DR-005 v2 without RB-DR005-V2-A1' fails three times — clause 3, clause 5, and the alternatives — and I confirmed the rider is genuinely present in adopted D-039, the entry I reviewed when that rider was drafted.

The attack 'grant extends to DR-006/007/009 before their selections' fails on measured fact: I scanned every adopted entry and none selects Route B for DR-006, DR-007 or DR-009, and D-001 assigns all three route A. The attack 'grant extends to DR-010 or condition 5' fails: D-001 assigns DR-010 route C, clause 5 now reads 'DR-010 remains Route C and is not this file', and clause 4 forbids authorizing docs/v2/implementation/.

All ten eligible-row pairings in clause 5 reproduce against adopted entries: DR-002 with D-047 and D-049, DR-003 with D-030 and D-041, DR-004 with D-048 and D-050, DR-005 with D-028 and D-039, DR-008 with D-029 and D-040.
The attack 'file 08 edited' fails: file 08 measures unchanged and git reports docs/v2/architecture and COORDINATOR-DECISIONS.md clean, with zero modified tracked files.

I checked what the revision removed, not only what it added. A token-loss pass from the previously cleared bytes to these returns NOTHING, and the clause 1 through clause 3 span hashes identically in both files at be6af59ca72afcc1b639cfbc. The six lines diff reports as removed are each replaced by a superset: 'DR-010 remains Route C.' becomes 'DR-010 remains Route C and is not this file.', and 'separate act.' becomes 'separate act. This entry does not adopt product-boundary-preview.v1 or any other product successor.' Every addition narrows scope.

Examined and declined, measured rather than judged from memory: the entry carries no 'Conditions 2–5 remain' or 'Condition 5 remains the only implementation authorization' sentence, which many sibling entries do. I counted across the 41 adopted entries: each phrase appears in 10 of them. At roughly a quarter it is not a convention this entry departs from, and clause 4's 'It may not authorize docs/v2/implementation/' plus the header's matching refusal cover the operative constraint for the act being bounded.

Examined and declined: the entry's history paragraph says the turn-1 file 'moved during review (bb806328 → cab483b5)', while my turn-1 verdict recorded that the divergence predated my measurement window — start and end were identical at cab483b5. The phrasing describes motion within the turn-1 review cycle rather than within my measurement window, which is defensible, and the operative disposition row characterizing my finding is accurate.
whatIDidNotCheck: The Codex reviews of D-057 at either turn. Not read; the turn-1 file was hashed without opening and the turn-2 file is absent at review time. The disposition table records six Codex findings, ADV-D057-T1-01 through T1-06, four of them accepted as 'not applicable here'. I verified the resulting bytes — this file is mechanics rather than Route C, adopts no product successor, and leaves DR-010 to a later ID — but not that those dispositions match what Codex actually raised.
The bytes the turn-1 dispatch pinned at bb806328, described here as an unrelated Route C product-boundary draft. They exist nowhere I can find, so I cannot confirm that characterization.

Whether adopted D-054 in fact confers the authority these mechanics presuppose. D-054 is not my subject; I objected to its coordinator-composed drafts separately, and this entry correctly points at the adopted user amendment rather than re-granting, so that question travels with D-054.
Whether product-boundary-preview.v1, named in clause 6's refusal, exists or what it contains. The entry only refuses to adopt it.

consentNote: I CONSENT with zero MUST-FIX and zero SHOULD-FIX. The subject held frozen at the dispatched digest through every measurement, which is what my turn-1 objection asked for and what the last three dispatches in this family had failed to deliver. On content I did not lean on having cleared the predecessor bytes: I re-derived all six digests, all ten pairings, the rider, the three row exclusions, and I checked what the revision removed as well as what it added — nothing removed, clauses 1-3 byte-identical, every addition narrowing. Where I was tempted to fault the entry for omitting the 'Conditions 2–5 remain' sentence, I counted instead and found it in 10 of 41 adopted entries, which makes it no convention. My single note is about the review process rather than these bytes, and it is meant as signal on where the freeze control still needs to reach.
